Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
7 October 2026 .
Brent $ 100.99 + 0.11 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters and KSLM Radio report an Iranian official says illegal routes in the Strait of Hormuz will soon be blocked.

02 gCaptain and Reuters report tanker attacks in the strait last week reached their highest level of any week since the Iran war began.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; Brent stood at $100.99 as of 19:44 UTC.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains under acute pressure. Reuters and KSLM Radio report that an Iranian official says the routes Iran designates as illegal, specifically the southern corridor hugging Oman's coast, will soon be blocked; the announcement echoes parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's October 4 statement, per background reporting, that the strait will not reopen until Iran's seven conditions are met. On the attack tempo, gCaptain and Reuters report last week's strike activity reached its highest level of any week since the Iran war began; gCaptain and Reuters also carry a report that 12 crew members were injured in a separate tanker strike, an incident the site has tracked since October 6. The Maran Gas Mystras, the Greek-flagged LNG carrier controlled by Angelicoussis Shipping Group that Hellenic Shipping News reports was struck by an unidentified projectile while leaving the strait, remains in the feed with no new details this window. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $100.99, up 0.11% over 24 hours, as of 19:44 UTC; 55 events have been indexed in the last 24 hours. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
